newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two dead as Typhoon Violet hits central Japan.
newsitem.headline: Two dead as Typhoon Violet hits central Japan.

text.p: At least two people were killed and 35 were injured in central Japan on Sunday when Typhoon Violet stormed along the country's Pacific coast.

Rail traffic in and around Tokyo was paralysed and Shinkansen bullet train services halted. Packing maximum winds of 126 kph (79 mph), Violet flattened trees and pylons, blowing off roof tiles and triggering landslides in central Japan.
Police said a total of two deaths and 35 injuries were reported. At least seven people including two surfers were unaccounted for.
A 64-year-old woman died and three people were injured in Kanagawa prefecture, southwest of Tokyo, when their car was hit by a tree blown down by gusty winds, police said.

In Fukushima prefecture, 150 km (95 miles) north of Tokyo, a six-year-old boy was killed when his house was crushed by a landslide, police said. In Tokyo, six people were injured when they were struck by flying pieces of glass.
As of 0900 GMT, Violet was 230 km (145 miles) northeast of Tokyo and moving northeast at 55 kph (35 mph), the agency said.
Because of Violet, the 17th typhoon to hit Japan this year, at least 195 domestic flights, 22 international flights and scores of ferry services were cancelled, authorities said.
The typhoon caused blackouts to more than 70,000 homes, flooded some 700 homes and partly damaged more than 50 homes in central Japan. The agency predicted rainfall of up to 50 cm (20 in).
